Profitability moved the wrong way: operating income of $20,890 million implies a 12.7% operating margin, while net income of $14,160 million yields an 8.6% net margin, down from fiscal 2024's 9.3% net margin on $14,806 million of net income ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Home_Depot)); management's adjusted operating margin also slipped year over year, confirming the GAAP trend ([ir.homedepot.com](https://ir.homedepot.com/)). Boeing delivered a dramatic turnaround in fiscal 2025 ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/BA.N/)). Revenue rebounded to $89,463M, up 34.5% from $66,517M in fiscal 2024, which had declined 14.5% ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing)). Profitability swung sharply: net income reached $2,235M (a 2.5% net margin) after a net loss of $11,817M in fiscal 2024 (a -17.8% net margin). Operating income of $4,289M produced a 4.8% operating margin, signaling progress under CEO Kelly Ortberg's recovery plan, though profitability remains thin relative to the company's $89.5B revenue base. With 182,000 employees and production ramping across the 737 MAX, 777X and 787 programs, Boeing's 2025 results mark its return to the black, but sustaining margin expansion will be the key watch item into fiscal 2026 ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ba/company/)).

Amazon closed FY2025 (ended 2025-12-31) with revenue of $716,900 million, a 12% revenue growth rate, producing $79,980 million of operating income and $77,670 million of net income — an operating margin of 11.2% and a net margin of 10.8% [en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_(company)). This extends the margin expansion begun in FY2024 (ended 2024-12-31), when revenue of $637,959 million (11.0% growth) generated $68,593 million of operating income and $59,248 million of net income, a 9.3% net margin. Operating margin improved roughly 45bps year-over-year while net margin expanded ~155bps, reflecting AWS scale, advertising momentum, and cost discipline across the North America and International segments. With trailing results still accelerating — Fortune reports LTM revenue of $775,680 million and profits of $135,281 million [fortune.com](https://fortune.com/company/amazon-com/) — profitability trajectory remains the key equity story alongside AWS and AI-driven cloud demand.

Alphabet closed FY2025 (ended 2025-12-31) with revenue of $402,800M ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphabet_Inc.)), up 15.1% from FY2024, while operating income was $129,000M and net income was $132,200M, yielding a 32.0% operating margin and 32.8% net margin. In FY2024 (ended 2024-12-31), Alphabet generated $350,018M of revenue, $112,390M of operating income (32.1% operating margin), and $100,118M of net income (28.6% net margin), with diluted EPS of $8.04 and operating cash flow of $125,299M. The FY2025 profitability step-up — net margin expanding roughly 420bps despite a larger revenue base — reflects Cloud and AI monetization gains. Concentration remains a watch item: Google advertising contributed $294,700M, about 73% of total revenue, so ad-market softness is the key downside risk to the margin trajectory.
